content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm having another issue. I'm using a [article_no] device and can't get the inputs to function correctly in online mode. Inputs I1 and I2 work, but none of the others respond. Am I missing something?
Have you checked if the clamps are secure?
I'm connecting a wire from a 12V source and clamping it into each terminal. All connections are tight, and I1 & I2 work, but the rest do not.
I have a brand new [article_no] device in my vehicle. I'll replace the current unit to see if that resolves the issue.
It turned out to be a faulty unit. After swapping with a new one, everything works properly. The defective device was only a few weeks old and will be sent back to [company_name].

You can also check the internal status of [product_name] without tools. If a text block is active, press the Cursor Down key several times until the time and date display appears. With just the date and time showing (no active text blocks), press the Cursor Right or Left key. This will show the actual status of all inputs connected to [product_name], regardless of whether they're used in the program. Pressing the cursor again cycles through outputs, markers, analog inputs, and analog outputs, allowing you to monitor the signals used by [product_name]. This is very useful for troubleshooting.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered issues detecting inputs on a specific [product_name] device. Although two digital inputs functioned correctly, others did not, prompting suspicion of hardware malfunction. Replacing the hardware fixed the problem, emphasizing the importance of device reliability and quality control. Additional guidelines for manual troubleshooting were provided, highlighting the need for accessible diagnostic features.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect all digital inputs of the [product_name] device to work reliably and to be able to easily identify and troubleshoot any malfunctions.
